title: Quickstart
text: Quickstart The repository samples build the native artifacts once. Choose a local GGUF model and pass its path to each text demo. Prerequisites Python 3.9+, Rust 1.82+, Node 22+, .NET 8+, CMake, and a native C/C++ toolchain. PowerShell · repository root Copy py samples/build.py native py samples/run.py ts --model C:/models/model.gguf py samples/run.py python --model C:/models/model.gguf py samples/run.py csharp --model C:/models/model.gguf py samples/run.py rust --model C:/models/model.gguf For the browser studio, build the independent WASM path: Browser / WASM Copy python samples/build.py web python samples/run.py web

title: Architecture
text: Architecture The core receives state and typed questions. An adapter renders the model's real prompt and tokenizer, returns candidate scores, and lets TurboJev validate, normalize, calibrate, and build the response. state text · JSON · media → typed questions choice · noul · score → TurboJev core plan · score · respond → EvaluationResponse same shape everywhere Core owns Schema and candidate validation Execution planning and calibration metadata Typed response construction Order robustness and parity contracts Adapters own Chat template and tokenizer GGUF, Transformers.js, or custom runtime Media preprocessing and hardware Process, file, and network boundaries

title: Core API
text: Typed fields: generate, JSON scalar schemas, dependencies and thinking Core API Operation Use it for Returns evaluate(request) Several typed questions or media EvaluationResponse evaluateCompatible(profile, request) Versioned compatibility contracts profile response Canonical request Copy { "state": {"message": "My package arrived broken."}, "questions": { "route": { "type": "choice", "instructions": "Which team should handle this?", "criteria": {"billing": "Payments", "shipping": "Delivery", "technical": "Product issue"} }, "urgent": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Needs human intervention?"} } } For small models, express the decision-relevant facts directly, keep each question to a clear decision, and enforce hard constraints in the host. See the decision-design guide for practical examples and validation advice.

title: Typed fields
text: Typed fields generate adds JSON-typed fields to TurboJev's portable core. evaluate remains the direct choice , noul and ordered score API. Finite fields score model candidates; unrestricted strings and numbers generate a bounded value. Extraction therefore generates tokens and can take longer than a single candidate decision. Request and response python Copy from turbojev import TurboJev with TurboJev.load("invoice.gguf", device="cpu", n_ctx=8192, n_seq_max=1) as client: response = client.generate( context="Invoice total: 324.50 GBP. Payment is overdue.", questions={ "total": {"type": "number", "instructions": "What is the total in GBP?"}, "overdue": {"type": "boolean", "instructions": "Is payment overdue?"}, "reminder": {"type": "string", "when": {"overdue": True}, "depends_on": ["total"], "instructions": "Write one short payment reminder."}, }, thinking=False, text_max_tokens=128, numeric_max_tokens=64, ) print(response["result"]) print(response["skipped"], response["usage"]) The same JSON request is accepted by every binding. Supply exactly one of questions (a field map) or schema (an object with properties , optional required , and optional additionalProperties: false ). All declared properties are requested; required validates property names, not a separate omission policy. Conditions control omissions. The schema subset supports scalar fields, not nested objects or arrays. state is an input alias for context . Field option Behavior type string , integer , number , boolean , or [type, "null"] ; retains JSON types enum 1–24 unique values of that type; a singleton is a constant with no model scoring instructions / description Question; description is the fallback depends_on Names of earlier results to include as plain values; forward references allowed when AND of tests on prior fields; adds implicit dependencies return_probabilities Boolean, finite fields only; returns a value/confidence/distribution wrapper permutations Explicit enums only: positive integer, auto , or all thinking Per-field override: false, true, or auto thinking_effort none , low (512 tokens), medium (2048), high (4096) thinking_budget Positive token budget, up to 32768; alternative to effort Token limits are request-level text_max_tokens (default 256) and numeric_max_tokens (default 64), each 1–32768. Booleans default to [true, false] , plus actual null for nullable booleans. Numeric equality distinguishes booleans from integers and does not round distinct 64-bit integer values. Unsupported keywords, including bounds, string length/format constraints and nested schemas, are rejected before inference rather than ignored. Invalid generated output and exhausted budgets are errors. Wllama 3.8.1 exposes top-N vocabulary scores and its Jinja autoparser does not apply custom GBNF on this path. The adapter resolves letter labels through the loaded model tokenizer using textual logit-bias keys, applies the same additive offset to every permitted label, and requests post-sampling probabilities with truncation disabled. A common offset preserves candidate log-odds and the conditional distribution; it does not favor the first option or select a winner. This uses one model call for 2–24 candidates. Missing or invalid scores are errors, never invented probabilities. The browser adapter does not claim a selective output head. Dependencies, conditions and null Dependencies form a validated acyclic graph. A dependent prompt receives only its named previous answers, without probability wrappers. The media envelope and its bytes stay intact. Fields currently execute serially in dependency order; this API does not promise shared-prefix batching or parallel field generation. Response fields return in caller order. json Copy { "context": "The account has seven overdue invoices.", "questions": { "count": {"type": "integer", "instructions": "How many invoices?"}, "escalate": {"type": "boolean", "when": {"count": {"gte": 5}}, "instructions": "Should support escalate this account?"}, "reference": {"type": ["string", "null"], "instructions": "Return the payment reference, or null when it is absent."} } } Tests support equality, list membership, and objects with in , not_in , ne , gt , gte , lt , lte . Comparison operands are type-checked. Open string fields may be tested for null, but not arbitrary string equality. A false condition skips the field and all its dependents without inference, including automatic effort selection. Skipped fields are absent from result and named in skipped ; they are not invented null answers. Actual null is present in result . The string "null" stays a string. Probabilities and permutation budgets json Copy {"type":"string","enum":["heads","tails"],"instructions":"Which side of a fair coin will appear?","permutations":"all","return_probabilities":true} The result wrapper contains value , confidence , probabilities and distribution . distribution is an array of {value, probability} retaining actual JSON types. Map keys normally use string values or JSON spellings for other scalars. In nullable string enums, the literal string "null" uses the quoted map key "\"null\"" to distinguish it from actual null's "null" key. Prefer the typed array if keys matter. Each ordering receives a real model evaluation. Scores are normalized separately, remapped to original values, then **probabilities** are averaged. auto uses canonical ordering and a Williams design: N evaluations for an even N, 2N for an odd N greater than one. Integer budgets sample distinct orderings reproducibly using request seed ; the identity is included. all visits every permutation. A hard cap of 720 prevents accidental factorial workloads. A six-sided die with all costs 720 evaluations; opt in deliberately. Averaging may reduce position bias but does not guarantee correct reasoning or calibrated confidence. This policy is separate from evaluate 's older opt-in cyclic logit averaging. Thinking and runtime capabilities Default generate thinking is false, independently of the load-time policy used by evaluate . A field can override the request. Budget-only field overrides inherit the request's on/off setting. Effort selects the setting explicitly. Contradictory settings fail validation. auto asks the model to choose none/low/medium/high as an additional hidden finite decision, exposes that selection in thinking_effort , and then performs the actual field request. It cannot also specify a fixed effort or budget. Runtime Finite fields Text/numbers Reasoning Native llama.cpp/GGUF Candidate logits JSON grammar plus Rust type checks Bounded text-model reasoning using the model's actual template Browser llama.cpp/WASM Candidate log probabilities JSON Schema grammar plus Rust type checks Explicit unsupported error Transformers.js text Token logits Bounded greedy generation, validated afterward; no grammar mask Explicit unsupported error Existing custom scorer/fixture Finite scoring Requires implementing infer_field / inferField Requires that hook Native and browser GGUF field generation accept the existing image/audio/video-frame envelope when the loaded model and matching projector support the modality. That is not a promise of receipt-reading accuracy. Native media reasoning is explicitly unsupported. Video inputs are decoded, timestamped image frames; TurboJev does not decode video containers or invoke external media executables. Current published native binaries cover Windows x86/x64/ARM64; portable source and WASM support do not imply Linux/macOS binary releases or execution on every architecture. usage.decisions counts completed output fields, not hidden effort queries or permutation evaluations. input_tokens sums known actual model counts; generated_tokens counts actual generated reasoning/value tokens. thinking contains actual model reasoning where supported. Increase context and reduce nSeqMax for longer reasoning. Unsupported modes, context overflow and unfinished reasoning return errors; no fallback answer is fabricated. Binding calls Language Method Rust engine.generate(GenerateRequest) ; types in turbojev::schema::fields Python client.generate(request) or client.generate(context=..., questions=...) Node/TypeScript await client.generate(request) ; exported GenerateRequest / GenerateResponse Browser await client.generate(request) or await wasmEngine.generate_json(JSON.stringify(request)) .NET await engine.GenerateJsonAsync(JsonSerializer.Serialize(request)) C tj_engine_generate_json(handle, json, &output) then tj_string_free(output) Android engine.generate(JSONObject(request)) Swift try engine.generate(json) on its managed affinity thread The native ABI is shim version 10; rebuild native dependents together. Runtime options are scoped to each field and restored after errors. Native nSeqMax=1 uses independent reference scoring for multiple questions. Shared-prefix reuse needs at least two sequences; parallel suffix reuse needs at least three. Scheduling changes do not switch the configured CPU/GPU device. Existing evaluate requests and responses remain supported. Tests and evals adapted from TypeLLM Reference tests TurboJev coverage Schema, nullable, grammar fields, text Scalar and enum typing, duplicate/invalid values, null wire presence, bounded native grammar generation Dependencies, conditions Forward references, cycles, typed operators, plain prior values, skipped descendants, skipped auto effort, media-envelope preservation Permutations, probabilities Unique seeded samples, Williams positions/neighbours, normalization and probability averaging, typed null distribution Thinking Validated flags, efforts and budgets, actual hidden effort calls, runtime errors rather than fabricated reasoning Images Existing media contracts plus field-generation path; model accuracy is measured separately Batching, concurrency, prefill, serving protocols Existing TurboJev worker/affinity and runtime tests remain; TypeLLM's SGLang-specific batching, remote-server and logprob-transport tests are not claimed as implemented here Run cargo test --workspace --locked and the browser runtime tests. evals/run.py records real numeric and JevBench model quality, errors, provenance and latency. TypeLLM's numeric cases and the three example ports have attribution and licenses; its published model results are not reused as TurboJev evidence.

title: Rust
text: Rust Native, strongly typed integration with the crates directly. crates.io ↗ Cargo.toml Copy [dependencies] turbojev = "0.28.3" turbojev-runtime-llamacpp = "0.28.3" Make a decision main.rs Copy use turbojev::TurboJev; use turbojev_runtime_llamacpp::{ffi::{FfiLlamaCpp, NativeConfig}, reference_backend, ReferencePromptConfig, ReferencePromptRenderer}; fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> { let runtime = FfiLlamaCpp::open("./model.gguf", NativeConfig::default())?; let renderer = ReferencePromptRenderer::new(ReferencePromptConfig::new( "my-app-v1", "Choose exactly one allowed code.", "Which team should handle this?")); let engine = TurboJev::new(reference_backend(renderer, runtime)); let request = turbojev::schema::EvaluationRequest { model: None, state: serde_json::json!({"message": "My package arrived broken."}), questions: [("department".to_owned(), turbojev::schema::Question::choice( "Which department should handle this?", [("billing".to_owned(), "Payments".to_owned()), ("shipping".to_owned(), "Delivery".to_owned()), ("other".to_owned(), "Other".to_owned())].into_iter().collect(), ))].into_iter().collect(), }; let answer = engine.evaluate(request)?; println!("{:?}", answer.answers); Ok(()) } Runnable source: samples/TurboJev-rust ↗

title: Node / TypeScript
text: Node / TypeScript Worker-backed native calls with typed results and clean async shutdown. npm ↗ npm install @turbojev/node Copy decision.ts Copy import { TurboJev } from "@turbojev/node"; const jev = await TurboJev.load({model: "./model.gguf", nGpuLayers: 0, nThreads: 4}); try { const result = await jev.evaluate({state: {message: "My package arrived broken."}, questions: {department: {type: "choice", instructions: "Which department should handle this?", criteria: {billing: "Payments", shipping: "Delivery", technical: "Product issue", other: "Other"}}}}); console.log(result.answers.department); } finally { await jev.close(); } Text and media source: TS sample ↗ Evaluate an image Use a multimodal runtime rather than a text-only GGUF model. The sample runner configures the SmolVLM2 worker for you. Terminal Copy python samples/multimodal/setup.py vision python samples/run.py ts --media photo.jpg --modality image --question "What animal is shown?" --options "A cat" "A dog" Once the engine is configured with that runtime, pass the same media envelope to evaluate : media.ts Copy import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises"; const result = await engine.evaluate({ state: { contract: "turbojev.media.v1", modality: "image", base64: (await readFile("photo.jpg")).toString("base64"), }, questions: { scene: { type: "choice", instructions: "What animal is shown?", criteria: { cat: "A cat", dog: "A dog" }, }, }, }); console.log(result.answers.scene);

title: Python
text: Python A context-managed API that returns ordinary dictionaries. PyPI ↗ pip install turbojev Copy decision.py Copy from turbojev import TurboJev with TurboJev.load("./model.gguf", n_gpu_layers=0) as jev: result = jev.evaluate({ "state": {"message": "My package arrived broken."}, "questions": {"department": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which department should handle this?", "criteria": {"billing": "Payments", "shipping": "Delivery", "technical": "Product issue", "other": "Other"}}}, })["answers"]["department"] print(result["choice"]) print(result["probabilities"]) Runnable source: samples/TurboJev-Python ↗

title: C ABI
text: C ABI Stable UTF-8 JSON ABI for C, Zig, Go, and other FFI hosts. header ↗ smoke.c Copy #include "turbojev.h" #include <stdio.h> int main(void) { tj_engine *engine = NULL; if (tj_engine_open_json("{\"model\":\"./model.gguf\"}", &engine) != TJ_OK) return 1; char *json = NULL; const char *request = "{\"state\":{\"message\":\"My package arrived broken.\"},\"questions\":{\"route\":{\"type\":\"choice\",\"instructions\":\"Which team?\",\"criteria\":{\"billing\":\"Payments\",\"shipping\":\"Delivery\"}}}}"; int rc = tj_engine_evaluate_json(engine, request, &json); if (rc == TJ_OK) { puts(json); tj_string_free(json); } tj_engine_close(engine); return rc != TJ_OK; } The ABI uses opaque handles, explicit string ownership, and thread-local errors.

title: .NET / C#
text: .NET / C# NuGet package with native assets for three Windows architectures. NuGet ↗ dotnet add package TurboJev --version 0.28.3 Copy Program.cs Copy using TurboJev; await using var jev = await TurboJevEngine.LoadAsync(new { model = "./model.gguf", nGpuLayers = 0, nThreads = 4 }); var request = new { state = new { message = "My package arrived broken" }, questions = new { department = new { type = "choice", instructions = "Which department?", criteria = new { billing = "Payments", shipping = "Delivery", technical = "Product issue", other = "Other" } } } }; var json = await jev.EvaluateJsonAsync(JsonSerializer.Serialize(request)); Console.WriteLine(json); The package carries win-x86, win-x64, and win-arm64 native assets. Evaluate an image Prepare the SmolVLM2 worker and run the complete .NET sample. The runner supplies the worker environment and native library paths. Terminal Copy python samples/multimodal/setup.py vision python samples/run.py csharp --media photo.jpg --modality image --question "What animal is shown?" --options "A cat" "A dog" With a multimodal engine, serialize the portable request and call EvaluateJsonAsync : Media.cs Copy using System.Text.Json; var request = new { state = new { contract = "turbojev.media.v1", modality = "image", base64 = Convert.ToBase64String( await File.ReadAllBytesAsync("photo.jpg")), }, questions = new { scene = new { type = "choice", instructions = "What animal is shown?", criteria = new { cat = "A cat", dog = "A dog" }, }, }, }; Console.WriteLine(await engine.EvaluateJsonAsync( JsonSerializer.Serialize(request)));

title: Browser / WASM
text: Browser / WASM Run locally in a web worker with optional WebGPU. npm ↗ npm install @turbojev/web Copy app.ts Copy import { TurboJevWeb } from "@turbojev/web"; const jev = await TurboJevWeb.load({ model: "https://example.com/model.onnx", wasmModuleUrl: "/turbojev_wasm.js", runtimeModuleUrl: "/my-runtime.js", runtimeOptions: {device: "wasm", dtype: "q4"}, }); const result = await jev.evaluate({state: {message: "My package never arrived"}, questions: {route: {type: "choice", instructions: "Choose a team", criteria: {billing: "Billing", shipping: "Shipping", support: "Support"}}}}); console.log(result.answers.route); await jev.close(); Included vanilla studio: python samples/build.py web . Try the browser playground The playground runs real inference in a worker. Select the input type before loading a model. Unload the current model to change it. Downloads start only when you press Load. Model selection Input Models Method Text · ONNX Qwen2.5 0.5B, Qwen3 0.6B Transformers.js candidate-token logits Text · GGUF Qwen3 0.6B Q4_K_M llama.cpp WASM constrained-answer log-probabilities Image CLIP B/32, CLIP B/16 Image–text similarity Image · GGUF LFM2-VL 450M Q4_0 + mmproj llama.cpp WASM mtmd image input Audio CLAP HTSAT Sound–text similarity Audio · GGUF LFM2 Audio 1.5B Q8_0 + mmproj Wllama mtmd audio input; real Node/WASM probe passed, browser qualification pending Video CLIP or LFM2-VL GGUF Four ordered, timestamped frames; no audio track Media limits Files must be at most 24 MB. Audio is mixed to mono at 48 kHz and must be 10 seconds or shorter. Video must be 60 seconds or shorter; the llama.cpp path sends four ordered, timestamped frames to mtmd. This does not guarantee temporal understanding and ignores the audio track. Small models can return incorrect decisions. Runtime assets The package supplies the worker bridge. Host a compiled TurboJev WASM module and an adapter that implements the runtime contract at the URLs above. The repository includes Transformers.js and llama.cpp WASM adapters. The llama.cpp adapter loads a matching mmproj for supported image models and passes video as ordered, timestamped image frames. A native Windows x64 LFM2 Audio Q8_0 probe passed four real audio decisions with cyclic candidate-order handling. GGUF audio is forwarded when Wllama detects an audio encoder, with media before prompt text. Wllama 3.8.1 reserves workers for audio preprocessing. A real LFM2 Audio probe passed four decisions through the adapter and Rust core in Node/WASM; the corrected browser page still requires a fresh run. Cyclic order correction is optional and now applies to media decisions too. The local site uses py website/serve.py to set WebAssembly threading headers. Select the llama.cpp runtime and a GGUF model in the playground; the browser loads the model locally from Hugging Face. The samples/build.py web command prepares the TurboJev WASM assets. Troubleshooting If WebGPU is unavailable, select CPU. If initialization runs out of memory, unload the model and try a smaller GGUF quantization. Cancel terminates the worker. Model downloads may take several minutes and require enough browser memory.

title: Android + Swift
text: Android + Swift Both mobile bindings call the C ABI on a dedicated affinity thread. sources ↗ Kotlin Copy val jev = TurboJev.load( JSONObject("{\"model\":\"app/model.gguf\"}") ).join() val request = """{"state":{"message":"My package arrived broken"},"questions":{"department":{"type":"choice","instructions":"Which department?","criteria":{"billing":"Payments","shipping":"Delivery"}}}}""" val result = jev.evaluate(request).join() jev.close() Swift Copy let jev = try TurboJevEngine( optionsJSON: #"{"model":"model.gguf"}"# ) let json = try jev.evaluate(#"{"state":{"message":"My package arrived broken"},"questions":{"department":{"type":"choice","instructions":"Which department?","criteria":{"billing":"Payments","shipping":"Delivery"}}}}"#) try jev.close()

title: Multimodal
text: Multimodal TurboJev does not depend on a particular multimodal checkpoint. An application-selected runtime owns decoding and preprocessing; TurboJev validates the envelope and returns the typed decision. media evidence Copy { "state": {"contract": "turbojev.media.v1", "modality": "image", "base64": "<encoded bytes>"}, "questions": {"scene": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "What animal is shown?", "criteria": {"cat": "A cat", "dog": "A dog"}}} } Included workers SmolVLM2 covers image/video CPU decisions. LFM2.5-Audio covers spoken-intent decisions. vision sample Copy python samples/multimodal/setup.py vision python samples/run.py vision --file photo.jpg --modality image \ --question "What animal is shown?" --options "A cat" "A dog"
